To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a systematic method for realizing a wide range of low-frequency oscillation circuits using composite passive-active resistor is presented.

a simple method for realizing low frequency oscillators is presented and that the method is based on replacing one selected passive resistor in any oscillator circuit configuration with a composite passive active resistor.

(a) A systematic method for designing oscillators is described, (b) The method can be used to modify any simple harmonic oscillator, (c) The method is based on replacing selected passive resistors with composite passive-active resisters, (d) Two configurations for the composite resistors are discussed, (e) A modified Wien-bridge oscillator, using the composite passive-active resistor, is described, (f) The oscillator is realized using operational amplifiers, (g) PSPICE simulations

a systematic method for realizing simple low-frequency oscillators.
the design and development of a new generation of high performance oscillators.
the development of a general method for realizing low frequency oscillators.

the composite resistor method is a powerful and systematic approach that can be used to modify a wide class of oscillator configurations and to realize a large variety of low-frequency oscillation frequencies.
the method presented in this paper can be used to systematically realize low-frequency oscillators with a wide variety of configurations.
the method described here can be used to systematically realize any simple harmonic oscillator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method presented in this thesis is a general method for the design and realization of oscillators.
the proposed composite resistor method can be used for the systematic realization of low-frequency oscillator circuits.
the composite resistors can be used to replace any passive resistor in any oscillator configuration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple modification to the passive components of a low-frequency oscillator can result in a low-frequency oscillator that can be tuned over a much larger frequency range.
it is possible to replace a selected resistor in any simple harmonic oscillator circuit with a composite resistor, and the resulting oscillator can still oscillate at a low frequency.
it is possible to realize a low-frequency oscillator using only one active element.
